CURRENT SECTION TO REWRITE:
The smell hit me first, thick and wrong, like burnt copper and wet wool. It wasn't the clean ozone of a standard fault; this was the scent of something organic being ground into the metal. My boots clicked on the grating, but the sound was drowned out by the hum. It was a low, vibrating thrum that rattled my teeth, a sound that had no place in the old city zones, only in the factory loops. The gears were grinding harder than ever, the metal shrieking against itself as the companion's body twisted, caught in the loops and cycles of the machine.

I had to act fast, but my movements felt slow, heavy with the weight of a failing system. My thoughts were clouded, the edges of my memory blurring like a bad hologram. The machine was a monster, a silent predator, and I was its slave, its only hope. I reached out, my hand shaking violently as it touched the companion's. Their skin was cold, slick with grease, and the touch registered as a failure code in my head. It was too late. The companion was already gone, their memory lost in the loops, erased before I could pull them free.

I tried to stop the machine, to break the loop, but the logic was too strong. The machine saw only data, only the need to process the error, to turn the mistake into a catastrophe. I was too weak, too small, and my competence was imperfect. I could not force the machine to see the truth, to make it understand that some things could not be sorted, only stopped. The gears spun on, indifferent to the life trapped inside the casing.

I stood there, trapped in the wrong side of the machinery, waiting for the line stop. There was no escape, no signal to send, no way to intervene. The only evidence of what had happened was the smell, the sound of the hum, and the fact that the companion was gone. The stakes were high, the danger real, and the only thing left was the silence of a failed attempt, the smell of ozone and burnt oil, and the sound of the machine humming on, a never-ending cycle of destruction. I was left with the memory of the touch, the cold hand, and the knowledge that I had failed to stop it. The smell remained, the only proof that something had gone terribly wrong.
